items.title: Microsoft and Alphabet diverge: Azure up 48%, Microsoft trims capex; Alphabet posts negative free cash flow and falls about 10%
items.summary: Microsoft beat estimates, with Azure revenue up 48%. It lowered its full-year capex forecast to $170B from $175B, and its CFO said delays from third-party GPU providers will push some capacity into the first half of 2027. Alphabet missed on earnings and revenue and reported negative free cash flow of more than $9B. It kept 2026 capex guidance at $195-205B, and its shares fell about 10% in extended trading. Neocloud stocks (CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN) and Oracle also dropped. Hyperscaler capex is expected to top $1 trillion next year.
items.why_it_matters: Investors punish AI spending that does not show up as cash flow. GPU delivery delays are a new constraint on the build-out.

items.title: Amazon: AWS grows 39% but free cash flow turns deeply negative and shares fall over 6%
items.summary: AWS revenue rose 39% to $45.98B, above the $45.29B consensus. Management expects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Capex was $77.3B in the quarter, against a FactSet estimate of $58.7B, and Amazon held its 2026 capex forecast at $220B. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was negative $42.4B, the second straight quarter of negative free cash flow. Shares fell more than 6% in extended trading.
items.why_it_matters: Cloud demand is strong, but the market worries about the cash cost of the AI build-out.
